question: The cultural sport of Maharashtra, 'dahi-handi' is associated with which festival?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna Janmashtami**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Dahi-handi'** is a traditional sport celebrated as part of the Krishna Janmashtami festival, marking the birth of Lord Krishna.
 
• The sport is inspired by the childhood pastime of Lord Krishna, who was fond of stealing butter from hanging pots.
 
• It involves forming human pyramids to break an earthen pot filled with curd, butter, or buttermilk, hung at a significant height.
 
• The event is celebrated with great enthusiasm, especially in Maharashtra, where it has become a cultural hallmark.
 
• The day is also marked by devotional singing, dancing, and reenactments of Lord Krishna's childhood stories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Krishna Janmashtami**: Celebrated on the eighth day (Ashtami) of the Krishna Paksha (dark fortnight) in the month of Bhadrapada as per the Hindu calendar.
 
• **Govinda Pathaks**: Teams participating in the 'dahi-handi' event are referred to as Govindas or Govinda Pathaks, named after one of Lord Krishna's titles.
 
• **Safety Measures**: In recent years, safety guidelines have been introduced to prevent injuries during the formation of human pyramids.
 
• **Regional Variations**: While Maharashtra is famous for 'dahi-handi', similar customs are observed in other states under different names and forms.
 
• **UNESCO Recognition**: Efforts have been made to include Janmashtami celebrations in UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage to highlight its cultural significance.
